Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has an article on:
точка
Wikipedia bg

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈtɔt͡ʃkɐ]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɔt͡ʃkɐ
  • Syllabification(key): точ‧ка

Etymology 1

[edit]

Borrowed from Russian то́чка (tóčka), from Proto-Slavic *tъčьka. Eventually, displaced Etymology 2.

Noun

[edit]

то́чка • (tóčka) f (relational adjective то́чков, diminutive то́чица)

  1. dot, spot
  2. (mathematics) point
  3. (also figurative) point, place, location
    и́зходна то́чка ― ízhodna tóčka ― starting point
    то́чка на кипе́не ― tóčka na kipéne ― boiling point
  4. period, full stop (punctuation)
  5. item (e.g. in a list)
Declension
[edit]
Declension of то́чка
singular plural
indefinite то́чка
tóčka 		то́чки
tóčki
definite то́чката
tóčkata 		то́чките
tóčkite
Related terms
[edit]
  • то́чен (tóčen, “exact, precise”)
  • тъка́ (tǎká, “to weave”)
  • тъ́кмо (tǎ́kmo, “just”, adverb)

References

[edit]
  • “точка”, in Речник на българския език [Dictionary of the Bulgarian Language] (in Bulgarian), Sofia: Bulgarian Academy of Sciences, 2014
  • “точка”, in Речник на българския език [Dictionary of the Bulgarian Language] (in Bulgarian), Chitanka, 2010

Etymology 2

[edit]

то́ча (tóča, “to drain”) +‎ -ка (-ka)

Noun

[edit]

то́чка • (tóčka) f (obsolete)

  1. source, spring, spout (point where some flow starts from)
    Synonyms: чу́чур (čúčur), соп (sop)
Declension
[edit]
Declension of то́чка
singular plural
indefinite то́чка

tóčkata 		то́чките
tóčkite
Related terms
[edit]
  • и́зточник (íztočnik, “source”)
  • ток (tok, “current”)
  • (obsolete) то́чен (tóčen, “sprung”)

References

[edit]
  • Nayden Gerov; Тодор Панчев (1904), “то́чка”, in Рѣчникъ на Блъгарскꙑй язꙑкъ. Съ тлъкувание рѣчи-тꙑ на Блъгарскꙑ и на Русскꙑ. [Dictionary of the Bulgarian language] (in Bulgarian), volume 5, Plovdiv: Дружествена печꙗтница "Съгласие.", page 348

Macedonian

  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

  2. period, full stop
  3. item (e.g. in a list)

Pannonian Rusyn

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Carpathian Rusyn то́чка (tóčka), from Proto-Slavic *tъčьka. Displaced Old Slovak točka (“pin, stopper, tap (usually on a barrel); frame, rim of glasses”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈtɔt͡ʃka]
  • Rhymes: -ɔt͡ʃka
  • Hyphenation: точ‧ка

Noun

[edit]

точка (točka) f (diminutive точочка)

  1. dot
  2. full stop, period
  3. point
    точка патреня ― točka patrenja ― viewpoint

Declension

[edit]
Declension of точка (točka)
singular plural
nominative точка (točka) точки (točki)
genitive точки (točki) точкох (točkox)
dative точки (točki) точком (točkom)
accusative точку (točku) точки (točki)
instrumental точку (točku) точками (točkami)
locative точки (točki) точкох (točkox)
vocative точко (točko) точки (točki)

Derived terms

[edit]
adjectives
  • точкасти (točkasti)
nouns
  • два точки (dva točki)
  • точка и запята (točka i zapjata)

Related terms

[edit]
adjectives
  • точни (točni)
adverbs
  • точно (točno)

[edit]

  • Fejsa, M.; Šlemender, M.; Čelʹovski, S. (2022), “dot”, in Анґлийско-руски словнїк [English-Rusyn Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy; Ruska matka, →ISBN, page 92
  • Fejsa, M.; Šlemender, M.; Čelʹovski, S. (2022), “period”, in Анґлийско-руски словнїк [English-Rusyn Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy; Ruska matka, →ISBN, page 208
  • Fejsa, M.; Šlemender, M.; Čelʹovski, S. (2022), “stop”, in Анґлийско-руски словнїк [English-Rusyn Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy; Ruska matka, →ISBN, page 304

Russian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Slavic *tъčьka. Cognate with Lithuanian taškas.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈtot͡ɕkə]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

то́чка • (tóčka) f inan (genitive то́чки, nominative plural то́чки, genitive plural то́чек, relational adjective то́чечный, diminutive то́чечка)

  1. period, dot, full stop
  2. point
    то́чка прикоснове́ния ― tóčka prikosnovénija ― point of contact
  3. dot, (for Morse code; colloquially dit)
    • (Can we date this quote?), “Мой адрес - Советский Союз”:
      Вы, то́чки-тире́ телегра́фные, ищи́те на стро́йках меня́.
      Vy, tóčki-tirɛ́ telegráfnyje, iščíte na strójkax menjá.
      You, telegraphic dots and dashes, seek me on building sites.
  4. pixel
    Synonym: пи́ксель (píkselʹ)

  • → Yakut: туочука (tuočuka)

то́чка! • (tóčka!)

  1. enough!
